Current policy verdicts

A policy is a versioned subset of the approved controls, published under its own registry key so a consumer can read the one question it cares about. Both USTB policies were first confirmed on 2026-08-19 and are attested on registry v2 as EIP-712 reports a relayer submits.

disclosure-freshness:1

CONFIRMED

Disclosure freshness

Is the issuer still publishing the disclosures it says it publishes, on the cadence it declares? A listing monitor needs that answer, and should not be told nothing merely because a valuation has not settled yet.

Reports expire at the end of the UTC day and re-publish at the daily window. The terminal reads the registry at the block you ask, so what it shows is the chain's answer, not this page's memory of it.

Refused, then confirmed

A NAV value was provisional. Touchstone refused it. The same value later survived the required evidence interval, became confirmed, and changed the behaviour of a consumer contract — without any control being weakened in between.

2026-08-18

Refused

The NAV row was present and fresh, but it had not settled. The settlement policy asks for a NAV held unchanged by a capture at least 24 hours older and at least 2 business days settled, so it declined to answer from a figure the issuer could still restate.

The interval

Nothing was relaxed

No control was edited and no threshold lowered while the refusal stood. The approved USTB control set remained 5 controls under approval ledger 0x4f2c7dd5ea0cd09c3b0e9d51445873c65b882a1b3b3265c15979b598dab91dd1, signed by 0x537873b087654395CB0A487B50d0bFBe15fA16Bc. The run waited for evidence instead.

2026-08-19

Confirmed

The same NAV — 11.18316100 as of 2026-08-18 — survived the interval, and both policies published CONFIRMED: mainnet at block 68512680, testnet at block 38698679.

Consumer effect

A contract changed answer

The mainnet gate at 0xAac48DC261B04737FDCB101D5049395121034a83 answered (true, "allowed") for the disclosure-freshness key it pins from 2026-08-19 — verdicts expire at end of day UTC and renew at the daily window — and the action it guards executed on chain. The gate is immutable: its code did not change, its input did.

Publication history

Sequences are per registry key and per chain, and they only move forward. The asset report publishes to registry v1; each policy verdict publishes to registry v2 as a relayer-submitted EIP-712 attestation.

Sequence 3 corrects sequence 1 and carries sequence 1's epoch, so for a time the latest testnet publication pointed at an epoch older than sequence 2's. That is the correction model working as designed: a correction supersedes the sequence it names without rewriting it, and a reader follows the sequence, not the calendar.

Evidence authorities

3 issuer-published JSON endpoints stand behind every USTB verdict. Touchstone reads public Superstate disclosures; it is not a party to them.

USTB evidence sources
Source What a control may quote from it
superstate-ustb-nav-daily The daily NAV row: the per-share value and the date it is stated as of.
superstate-ustb-yield The published yield row and the date it is stated as of.
superstate-ustb-holdings The holdings disclosure and the date it is stated as of.

Every fetch is stored as a digest-addressed capture. A control quotes a byte span from a named capture rather than a value someone retyped, the report carries the evidence root over those captures, and a reader can recompute both offline from the signed bundle. How sources are audited →

The one scripted page is the Policy Terminal, whose code is served from this host and talks only to X Layer RPC endpoints. Every number and address on this site is rendered from one canonical data source at build time.
